heroHeadline: Pear Lake Fire Grows Past 166,000 Hectares as Two New Fires Ignite in Northwestern Ontario
heroSubtitle: British Columbia's Pear Lake fire, the season's second-largest, grew to 166,111 hectares as of August 30 — a slow but steady 1,366-hectare gain over six days as crews work planned ignitions and containment lines around Big Bar Mountain. In Northwestern Ontario, two small new fires were confirmed August 31 near Sioux Narrows and Blue Lake Provincial Park, though the region's active count held steady at 59 as other starts were closed out; the Rinker Lake Complex — Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34 and Dryden 35, a combined 377,198 hectares — remains not under control despite low fire activity, with command based at Thunder Bay Fire Management Headquarters. Canada remains at National Preparedness Level 5, with international crews from Mexico, Costa Rica, New Zealand and Australia still supporting Ontario and British Columbia. Nationally, 582 wildfires remain active (31 out of control) across 4,793 fires and 4.1 million hectares burned this season, per the federal government's most recent (Aug 18) figures. Five deaths remain confirmed this season.
